shell.trustedFrame: The shell owns money, membership, approvals, connected surfaces, and the canonical venture record.
shell.editableInterior: The interior can rewrite prompts, UI, agent structure, and venture code, but it should call back into the shell for trusted state changes.

interiorSource.note: Interior files live in Dev Scap today. Connected repos are execution surfaces and future mirror targets, not the source of truth yet.

connectionPoints.label: Treasury
connectionPoints.summary: Capital enters through the shell. The interior can read the pool and eventually request budget, but it cannot rewrite the ledger.
notes: Money becomes venture-usable when the shell records it.
Reservations and payouts should remain shell-mediated.

connectionPoints.label: Members
connectionPoints.summary: The shell keeps the roster and seats canonical. The interior can organize around people, but it cannot rewrite who belongs to the venture.
notes: Membership and identity stay trusted at the shell boundary.

connectionPoints.label: Approvals
connectionPoints.summary: The interior can open decisions, but the shell owns the approval record and the final attributed outcome.
notes: Approvals should land in the canonical record, not only inside venture UI.

connectionPoints.label: Canonical record
connectionPoints.summary: Work can happen anywhere. It becomes venture history only once it lands in the shell with provenance.
notes: Agents and members can create work, but the shell records what became real.

connectionPoints.label: Repo surfaces
connectionPoints.summary: Connected repos are execution surfaces and future mirror targets. The shell keeps the attachment clear while the interior stays editable.
notes: The connected repo is not the source of truth for the interior yet.
